source_1.citation: Edwards, E. A., G. Gebhart and O. E. Maughan. 1983. Habitat suitability information: smallmouth bass. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service FWS/OBS-82/10.36. 47 pp.
source_1.what: Suitability index (SI) curves for the Instream Flow Incremental Methodology. Curve set 20110 (Figure 11, 'spawning', category one) and 20105/20111 (Figures 10 and 12, 'incubation'). Category one curves are built from the literature and professional judgement, not from utilisation data; the preface states the models 'have not been tested against field data'.
source_1.how_read: digitised by eye from the scanned figure (govinfo PDF GOVPUB-I49-PURL-LPS101721, page 39 of the scan), breakpoints to about 0.05 ft/s and 0.05 in suitability
source_1.note: the spawning velocity curve is a mean-column velocity at the spawning site in the IFIM sense, comparable in kind to the 2 m cell's depth-averaged velocity used here; it is far more permissive (half suitability near 1.5 ft/s, 0.46 m/s) than the utilisation-based adult curve (half near 0.3 ft/s, 0.09 m/s)

source_2.citation: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Oklahoma Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit. 2020. Assessing the spawning movement and habitat needs of riverine Neosho Smallmouth Bass. CSS 145-2020 (final report; the nesting results are also in Miller et al. 2021, Diversity and Distributions 27, doi 10.1111/ddi.13250).
quotes: Nests were typically located at intermediate depths (mean = 0.8 m; SD = 0.3) and in low velocity habitats (0.0-0.2 m/s).

In total, 160 [nests] ... were 0.84 m (SD = 0.29) and 0.83 m (SD = 0.31), respectively. Nest-surface water velocities were 0.0-0.2 m/s, though most cluster nests (96%) and regular nests (96%) occurred in zero-velocity habitats.
For each nest observed, we measured water depth (0.01 m) and velocity at the nest surface (0.1 m/s, focal location at estimated nest center).
source_2.note: velocity at the nest surface with a 0.1 m/s resolution flow probe: a nest-scale quantity, like the single reading taken at each Huron nest (median 0.02 m/s), not the cell-scale velocity the chain predicts

source_3.citation: Dauwalter, D. C. and W. L. Fisher. 2007. Spawning chronology, nest site selection and nest success of smallmouth bass during benign streamflow conditions. American Midland Naturalist 158: 60-78.
source_3.quote: Males selected nest sites with intermediate water depths, low water velocity and near cover, behavior that is typical of smallmouth bass.
source_3.note: abstract only; the numbers are behind the paywall

how_the_prior_is_built: The velocity coefficient of the exponential relative-use model, S(v) = exp(b_v v), gets a Gaussian prior centred on the value that best fits the spawning SI curve of source 1 over 0 to 0.8 m/s, with a standard deviation large enough that the steep utilisation-based adult curve of the same document lies within two standard deviations: a weak prior that carries the sign and the order of magnitude and lets 59 nests move it. The depth coefficient gets a prior centred on the positive slope of the spawning depth curve over the nest depth range with a wide standard deviation. Bank distance has no published curve and keeps a weak zero-centred prior.
